event.title: Awareness Outbreak
event.summary: Marie-Celestin Karondwa, a politician from the ruling UDPS party in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, was beaten on Sunday after advocating for Ebola awareness during a radio interview. The incident occurred in Butembo, a region experiencing an Ebola outbreak, as residents reacted violently to his message promoting disease prevention measures.

timeline.title: Mobile Labs Enhance Ebola Testing Efficiency in Eastern DR Congo
timeline.summary: A mobile laboratory in Butembo, eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, has been operational for two weeks, significantly reducing the time required for Ebola test results. Previously, results took up to 72 hours, but the new facility can provide results within 24 hours, and in some cases, as quickly as six hours. This improvement is a relief for staff at the nearby Ebola treatment center.

timeline.title: Ebola Outbreak in DR Congo Exceeds 4,000 Deaths Amid Ongoing Challenges
timeline.summary: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has surpassed 4,000 deaths, according to health authorities. Efforts to control the epidemic are hampered by violence and public mistrust, exemplified by the recent burning of an Ebola-hit transit camp, which forced 19,000 people to flee.

timeline.title: Kenya Reports First Confirmed Ebola Case and Death Following Return from DRC
timeline.summary: Kenya has confirmed its first-ever case of Ebola, resulting in the death of a man who had recently returned from the Democratic Republic of Congo. Health authorities have identified 28 contacts of the deceased as they monitor the situation closely. The outbreak in the DRC has been severe, with over 4,000 deaths reported this year.

The patient died after returning from the DRC.
28 contacts have been traced by health authorities.

event_overview.title: About Awareness Outbreak
event_overview.subject: Awareness Outbreak
event_overview.summary: “Awareness Outbreak” is not an official outbreak designation in the sources consulted; the timeline appears to concern Ebola virus disease (EVD) reporting and response in and around the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). EVD outbreaks are public-health emergencies managed primarily by DRC health authorities with support from the World Health Organization (WHO) and partners, using testing, contact tracing, infection prevention, treatment, vaccination and community engagement.

facts.label: Disease and setting
facts.value: Ebola virus disease outbreaks in the DRC have involved Zaire ebolavirus; the country has experienced repeated outbreaks since Ebola was first identified there in 1976.

facts.label: Largest recent outbreak
facts.value: The DRC’s tenth Ebola outbreak ran from 1 August 2018 to 25 June 2020, affecting North Kivu, Ituri and South Kivu provinces; WHO recorded 3,470 confirmed and probable cases and 2,287 deaths.

facts.label: Cross-border relevance
facts.value: The 2018–2020 outbreak also had cross-border implications: four cases in Uganda were attributed to movement from the DRC and were included in the DRC death count in CDC reporting.

facts.label: Recent officially documented DRC outbrea
facts.value: WHO records that the April–July 2022 outbreak in Mbandaka, Équateur Province, involved five cases and five deaths, while an August–September 2022 event in Beni, North Kivu, involved one confirmed case; both were formally declared over after 42 days without further transmission following the last burial.

facts.label: Response model
facts.value: National authorities and WHO describe the core response as laboratory testing, contact tracing, infection prevention and control, treatment, vaccination where appropriate, safe burials and community engagement.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers particular claimed developments related to Ebola awareness, diagnostics, deaths and possible regional spread; it does not by itself establish that these items constitute one officially declared outbreak or validate their reported totals.
